written: 2026-11-21, after SeedLM-28, before the measure was run
question: Are coders that read the real training tasks in three wordings more independent voters? Only agreement between coders that learned differently has changed the ranking (SeedLM-10 to 20)
primary_measure: development fifth, coders alone: the vote of each 27-coder set (ties to the shortest program, mean over 200 orders; scripts/seedlm16_occam.py --coders). Supported if the paraphrase set beats the control set by at least 0.5 and the engine's 65; not supported if it does not beat the control set; inconclusive otherwise
secondary_measures: held-out teacher tasks, the same vote
the engine and each 27-coder set at equal weight (scripts/seedlm19_engine_ensemble.py --coders) against 69
choice: diagnostic; adoption only through the usual rule (above 69, then the validation gate)

outcome.primary: development fifth, coders alone: paraphrase set 64.76, control set 63.72 (24 coders: 64.72). The paraphrase set beats the control set by 1.04 but not the engine's 65: inconclusive (reports/seedlm/ensemble_occam_27p.json, _27c.json)
secondary: held-out teacher tasks: paraphrase set 70.62, control set 73.22 (24 coders: 72.17)
engine and ensemble at equal weight: 68 for both sets (1 fixed, 1 broken against the engine side's 68), against 69 (reports/seedlm/engine_ensemble_27p.json, _27c.json)
outcome.reading: Against the 24 coders, the paraphrase coders add nothing on the development tasks and cost 1.6 on the teacher tasks; the 80-minute controls cost 1.0 on the development tasks and add 1.1 on the teacher tasks. Neither set is a more independent voter in the sense that matters: the vote and its combination with the engine stay where they were
